source_text: וַ/תַּעֲלֵ֨/הוּ עִמָּ֜/הּ כַּ/אֲשֶׁ֣ר גְּמָלַ֗תּ/וּ בְּ/פָרִ֤ים שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ וְ/אֵיפָ֨ה אַחַ֥ת קֶ֨מַח֙ וְ/נֵ֣בֶל יַ֔יִן וַ/תְּבִאֵ֥/הוּ בֵית יְהוָ֖ה שִׁל֑וֹ וְ/הַ/נַּ֖עַר נָֽעַר־׃
english_snapshot: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bulls[a], one ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of Yahweh at Shiloh. Now the boy was young.

signals.text: The Masoretic text reads 'three bulls.' The Septuagint reads 'a three-year-old bull,' supported by the surviving age-related word in the published Hebrew transcription of 4QSam-a (4Q51); part of the surrounding animal phrase is supplied. These witnesses also include bread. Which textual form is earlier remains under review.

source_text: אַל תַּרְבּ֤וּ תְדַבְּרוּ֙ גְּבֹהָ֣ה גְבֹהָ֔ה יֵצֵ֥א עָתָ֖ק מִ/פִּי/כֶ֑ם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ל דֵּעוֹת֙ יְהוָ֔ה ו/לא נִתְכְּנ֖וּ עֲלִלֽוֹת־׃
english_snapshot: Do not keep speaking so very proudly; do not let arrogance come out of your mouth[a], for Yahweh is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.

signals.text: Or, following the consonantal text more strictly, 'and actions are not weighed.' The main text follows the traditional reading that the LORD evaluates human deeds.

source_text: רַגְלֵ֤י חסיד/ו יִשְׁמֹ֔ר וּ/רְשָׁעִ֖ים בַּ/חֹ֣שֶׁךְ יִדָּ֑מּוּ כִּֽי לֹ֥א בְ/כֹ֖חַ יִגְבַּר אִֽישׁ־־׃
english_snapshot: He guards the feet of his faithful ones[a], but the wicked are silenced in darkness[c][b], for not by strength does a man prevail.

signals.text: Hebrew textual tradition may also be read as singular, 'his faithful one'; the plural sense 'his faithful ones' is adopted because it fits the poetic parallelism and likely intended collective meaning.

source_text: א֣וֹי לָ֔/נוּ מִ֣י יַצִּילֵ֔/נוּ מִ/יַּ֛ד הָ/אֱלֹהִ֥ים הָ/אַדִּירִ֖ים הָ/אֵ֑לֶּה אֵ֧לֶּה הֵ֣ם הָ/אֱלֹהִ֗ים הַ/מַּכִּ֧ים אֶת מִצְרַ֛יִם בְּ/כָל מַכָּ֖ה בַּ/מִּדְבָּֽר־־׃
english_snapshot: Woe to us! Who can deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the wilderness[a][b].

signals.text: Hebrew: 'in the wilderness.' The phrase is difficult in context, since the plagues struck Egypt before Israel's wilderness journey; the translation follows the Masoretic Text as written.

source_text: וַ/יַּ֞ךְ בְּ/אַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית שֶׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֤י רָאוּ֙ בַּ/אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה וַ/יַּ֤ךְ בָּ/עָם֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֑ישׁ וַ/יִּֽתְאַבְּל֣וּ הָ/עָ֔ם כִּֽי הִכָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בָּ/עָ֖ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה־־
english_snapshot: And he struck down some of the men of Beth-shemesh because they had looked into the ark of Yahweh[a]. He struck down seventy men among the people, fifty thousand men[b], and the people mourned because Yahweh had struck the people with a great blow.

signals.text: The Hebrew reads, 'seventy men, fifty thousand men,' a difficult wording. It may mean 'seventy men out of fifty thousand men,' 'fifty thousand and seventy men,' or reflect a textual problem; some ancient witnesses support a much smaller number.

source_text: וַ/יַּ֨עַן אִ֥ישׁ מִ/שָּׁ֛ם וַ/יֹּ֖אמֶר וּ/מִ֣י אֲבִי/הֶ֑ם עַל כֵּן֙ הָיְתָ֣ה לְ/מָשָׁ֔ל הֲ/גַ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל בַּ/נְּבִאִֽים־׃
english_snapshot: Then a man from there answered and said[a], “And who is their father?” Therefore it became a proverb: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

signals.text: Or, “And who is his father?” Some translations take the question as referring specifically to Saul, but the Masoretic Text reads “their father.”

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵי/הֶ֜ם עֵ֧ד יְהוָ֣ה בָּ/כֶ֗ם וְ/עֵ֤ד מְשִׁיח/וֹ֙ הַ/יּ֣וֹם הַ/זֶּ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֧א מְצָאתֶ֛ם בְּ/יָדִ֖/י מְא֑וּמָה וַ/יֹּ֖אמֶר עֵֽד׃פ
english_snapshot: And he said to them[a], “Yahweh is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that you have found nothing in my hand.” And they said[c][b], “He is witness.”

signals.text: The final Hebrew verb is singular (“and he said”), but in context it functions as a collective response, hence “they said.”

source_text: בֶּן שָׁנָ֖ה שָׁא֣וּל בְּ/מָלְכ֑/וֹ וּ/שְׁתֵּ֣י שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל־־׃
english_snapshot: Saul was one year old when he became king[a], and he reigned two years over Israel.

signals.text: The Hebrew text here is difficult and likely textually deficient. Literally, 'Saul was a son of one year in his becoming king, and he reigned two years over Israel.' Some ancient witnesses and later proposals supply larger numbers, such as 'thirty' for Saul's age and 'forty-two' for the length of his reign.

source_text: וּ/פְלִשְׁתִּ֞ים נֶאֶסְפ֣וּ לְ/הִלָּחֵ֣ם עִם יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים אֶ֤לֶף רֶ֨כֶב֙ וְ/שֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ פָּרָשִׁ֔ים וְ/עָ֕ם כַּ/ח֛וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל שְׂפַֽת הַ/יָּ֖ם לָ/רֹ֑ב וַֽ/יַּעֲלוּ֙ וַ/יַּחֲנ֣וּ בְ/מִכְמָ֔שׂ קִדְמַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית אָֽוֶן׀־־־׃
english_snapshot: And the Philistines gathered to fight against Israel: thirty thousand chariots[a], and six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand that is on the seashore. They went up and camped at Mikmash, east of Beth-aven.

signals.text: Hebrew reads 'thirty thousand chariots.' Some interpreters and ancient witnesses have suggested a smaller number (for example, 'three thousand') because thirty thousand seems unusually large in context, but the main text follows the Masoretic Hebrew.

source_text: וַ/יָּ֣קָם שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל וַ/יַּ֛עַל מִן הַ/גִּלְגָּ֖ל גִּבְעַ֣ת בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וַ/יִּפְקֹ֣ד שָׁא֗וּל אֶת הָ/עָם֙ הַ/נִּמְצְאִ֣ים עִמּ֔/וֹ כְּ/שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִֽישׁ־־׃
english_snapshot: Then Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin[a], and Saul counted the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.

signals.text: Some witnesses and translations read “to Geba of Benjamin” instead of “to Gibeah of Benjamin.” The Hebrew text here reads “Gibeah of Benjamin.”

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ לַֽ/אֲחִיָּ֔ה הַגִּ֖ישָׁ/ה אֲר֣וֹן הָ/אֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּֽי הָיָ֞ה אֲר֧וֹן הָ/אֱלֹהִ֛ים בַּ/יּ֥וֹם הַ/ה֖וּא וּ/בְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל־׃
english_snapshot: Then Saul said to Ahijah[b][a], “Bring the ark of God here,” for the ark of God was that day with the sons of Israel.

signals.text: Some textual traditions and interpreters read “Bring the ephod” instead of “Bring the ark of God.” The Hebrew text here reads “ark of God.”

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֗וּל אֶל יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הָ֣בָ/ה תָמִ֑ים וַ/יִּלָּכֵ֧ד יוֹנָתָ֛ן וְ/שָׁא֖וּל וְ/הָ/עָ֥ם יָצָֽאוּ־׃
english_snapshot: Then Saul said to Yahweh, the God of Israel, “Give a perfect lot.”[a] And Jonathan and Saul were taken, but the people escaped.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'Give perfect/blameless.' The word 'lot' is supplied from the context. The Septuagint has a longer prayer asking why God has not answered and distinguishing guilt in Saul or Jonathan from guilt in the people. Its requests are commonly interpreted in terms of Urim and Thummim; these are not preserved Hebrew words in 4Q52 fragment 2, whose reconstruction and identification with this passage are disputed.

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל שָׁא֔וּל הֶ֚רֶף וְ/אַגִּ֣ידָה לְּ/ךָ֔ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖/י הַ/לָּ֑יְלָה ו/יאמרו ל֖/וֹ דַּבֵּֽר־׃ס
english_snapshot: Then Samuel said to Saul[a], “Stop, and I will tell you what Yahweh said to me last night.” And he said to him, “Speak.”

signals.text: Hebrew written form has 'and they said to him'; context indicates the speaker is Saul, so the sense is singular: 'and he said to him.'

source_text: וַ/יִּקַּ֨ח שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶת קֶ֣רֶן הַ/שֶּׁ֗מֶן וַ/יִּמְשַׁ֣ח אֹת/וֹ֮ בְּ/קֶ֣רֶב אֶחָי/ו֒ וַ/תִּצְלַ֤ח רֽוּחַ יְהוָה֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד מֵ/הַ/יּ֥וֹם הַ/ה֖וּא וָ/מָ֑עְלָ/ה וַ/יָּ֣קָם שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַ/יֵּ֖לֶךְ הָ/רָמָֽתָ/ה־־־׃ס
english_snapshot: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers[a]. And the Spirit of Yahweh rushed upon David from that day onward[b]. Then Samuel rose and went to Ramah.

signals.text: Or 'the spirit of the LORD rushed upon David.' English capitalization reflects interpretation; Hebrew manuscripts do not mark this distinction.

source_text: וַ/יֵּצֵ֤א אִֽישׁ הַ/בֵּנַ֨יִם֙ מִ/מַּחֲנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים גָּלְיָ֥ת שְׁמ֖/וֹ מִ/גַּ֑ת גָּבְה֕/וֹ שֵׁ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת וָ/זָֽרֶת־׃
english_snapshot: Then a champion came out from the camps of the Philistines[a]; his name was Goliath, from Gath. His height was six cubits and a span[b].

signals.text: The Masoretic Text reads “six cubits and a span,” approximately 9 feet 9 inches (about 3.0 meters), depending on the cubit used. 4QSama (4Q51) and the Septuagint read “four cubits and a span,” approximately 6 feet 9 inches (about 2.1 meters). The restoration assessment currently prefers four, but the main text remains synchronized to its recorded WLC source pending image verification and full critical-source promotion.

source_text: וַ/יָּקֻ֣מוּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל וִ/יהוּדָ֜ה וַ/יָּרִ֗עוּ וַֽ/יִּרְדְּפוּ֙ אֶת הַ/פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים עַד בּוֹאֲ/ךָ֣ גַ֔יְא וְ/עַ֖ד שַׁעֲרֵ֣י עֶקְר֑וֹן וַֽ/יִּפְּל֞וּ חַֽלְלֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ בְּ/דֶ֣רֶךְ שַׁעֲרַ֔יִם וְ/עַד גַּ֖ת וְ/עַד עֶקְרֽוֹן־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then the men of Israel and Judah rose up and shouted[a], and they pursued the Philistines as far as Gai and as far as the gates of Ekron. The slain Philistines fell along the road to Shaaraim[b], as far as Gath and as far as Ekron.

signals.text: Hebrew 'as far as the entrance to the valley.' The phrase is textually and syntactically difficult; some understand it as a place name or render it more literally but less clearly.

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹנָתָ֜ן אֶל דָּוִ֗ד יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּֽי אֶחְקֹ֣ר אֶת אָבִ֗/י כָּ/עֵ֤ת מָחָר֙ הַ/שְּׁלִשִׁ֔ית וְ/הִנֵּה ט֖וֹב אֶל דָּוִ֑ד וְ/לֹֽא אָז֙ אֶשְׁלַ֣ח אֵלֶ֔י/ךָ וְ/גָלִ֖יתִי אֶת אָזְנֶֽ/ךָ־־־׀־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And Jonathan said to David[a], “As Yahweh, the God of Israel, lives, when I sound out my father about this time tomorrow, or the third day, and behold, if it is favorable toward David[c][b], shall I not then send to you and uncover your ear?"

signals.text: The Hebrew wording is elliptical and difficult; the sense is a solemn oath or pledge invoking the LORD as witness.

source_text: וְ/שֵׁ֤ם הָ/אִישׁ֙ נָבָ֔ל וְ/שֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖/וֹ אֲבִגָ֑יִל וְ/הָ/אִשָּׁ֤ה טֽוֹבַת שֶׂ֨כֶל֙ וִ֣/יפַת תֹּ֔אַר וְ/הָ/אִ֥ישׁ קָשֶׁ֛ה וְ/רַ֥ע מַעֲלָלִ֖ים וְ/ה֥וּא כ/לב/ו־׃
english_snapshot: The man's name was Nabal[a], and his wife's name was Abigail. The woman was intelligent and beautiful in appearance, but the man was harsh and evil in his dealings; he was a Calebite.

signals.text: Hebrew probably means 'a Calebite,' that is, a member of Caleb's clan; the written form is unusual, and some note the possibility of reading it differently.

source_text: כֹּה יַעֲשֶׂ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לְ/אֹיְבֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד וְ/כֹ֣ה יֹסִ֑יף אִם אַשְׁאִ֧יר מִ/כָּל אֲשֶׁר ל֛/וֹ עַד הַ/בֹּ֖קֶר מַשְׁתִּ֥ין בְּ/קִֽיר־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: May God do so to David’s enemies[a], and more also[b], if by morning I leave so much as one male of all who belong to him.

signals.text: Some interpreters understand 'David’s enemies' as a scribal euphemism for 'David' (or 'me'), since the usual oath formula is self-imprecatory.

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֕אמֶר לָ֥/מָּה זֶּ֛ה אֲדֹנִ֥/י רֹדֵ֖ף אַחֲרֵ֣י עַבְדּ֑/וֹ כִּ֚י מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתִי וּ/מַה בְּ/יָדִ֖/י רָעָֽה־׃
english_snapshot: And he said[a], “Why is my lord pursuing his servant like this? For what have I done[b], and what evil is in my hand?”

signals.text: Hebrew: 'his servant.' Some translations read 'your servant' to smooth the direct address, but the Masoretic Text has the third-person form.

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֣אמֶר אָכִ֔ישׁ אַל פְּשַׁטְתֶּ֖ם הַ/יּ֑וֹם וַ/יֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד עַל נֶ֤גֶב יְהוּדָה֙ וְ/עַל נֶ֣גֶב הַ/יַּרְחְמְאֵלִ֔י וְ/אֶל נֶ֖גֶב הַ/קֵּינִֽי־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then Achish said[a], “Where have you made a raid today?” And David said, “Against the Negev of Judah, against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites[b], and against the Negev of the Kenites.”

signals.text: Hebrew text literally reads something like 'Did you not raid today?' but the sense in context is interrogative: 'Where have you made a raid today?'

english_snapshot: And Yahweh has done for you just as he spoke by my hand: Yahweh has torn the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbor[b][a], to David.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'has done for himself.' Many translations read 'has done to you' or 'for you,' smoothing the sense toward Saul; the Masoretic Text here reads 'for him/for himself.'

source_text: וַ/יַּ֜עַן כָּל אִֽישׁ רָ֣ע וּ/בְלִיַּ֗עַל מֵֽ/הָ/אֲנָשִׁים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלְכ֣וּ עִם דָּוִד֒ וַ/יֹּאמְר֗וּ יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא הָלְכ֣וּ עִמִּ֔/י לֹֽא נִתֵּ֣ן לָ/הֶ֔ם מֵ/הַ/שָּׁלָ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִצַּ֑לְנוּ כִּֽי אִם אִ֤ישׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּ/וֹ֙ וְ/אֶת בָּנָ֔י/ו וְ/יִנְהֲג֖וּ וְ/יֵלֵֽכוּ־־־־־־־־־׃ס
english_snapshot: Then every wicked and worthless man from among the men who had gone with David answered and said[a], “Because they did not go with me, we will not give them any of the spoil that we recovered[c][b], except that each man may take his wife and his children and lead them away and go.”

signals.text: Hebrew 'with me'; the speakers are a group, but the quotation preserves the singular form in the source text.

source_text: וַ/יָּ֣מָת שָׁא֡וּל וּ/שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת בָּנָי/ו֩ וְ/נֹשֵׂ֨א כֵלָ֜י/ו גַּ֧ם כָּל אֲנָשָׁ֛י/ו בַּ/יּ֥וֹם הַ/ה֖וּא יַחְדָּֽו־׃
english_snapshot: So Saul died[a], and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, and all his men[b], together on that day.

signals.text: Some Greek witnesses read 'all his armor' instead of 'all his men.' The Hebrew text supports 'all his men.'
